item.title: Jim Mora's coaching staff had a significant, and bizarre, mid-game change
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Two-time former NFL head coach Jim Mora had an interesting experience on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
Two-time former NFL head coach Jim Mora had an interesting experience on Saturday.

Mora, in his first year as the head coach at Colorado State, took play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Tyson Summers during a game against Oregon State. Summers responded by leaving.

For good.

"Tyson was relieved of his play-calling duties, he left the field, and he is no longer with this football program," Mora said after the game, via Zac Al-Khateeb of USA Today. "That is permanent."

Mora made it clear that he didn't fire Summers.

"That wasn't anything that I would ever consider," Mora said. "I just relieved him of his duties as a play-caller. He made the decision to leave the field on his own. He's no longer with the program."

The change happened after Oregon State scored on each of its first two drives. Associate head coach and defensive line coach Kenny McClendon took over Summers's duties.

On the first play called by McClendon, Colorado State forced a turnover that led to a touchdown that tied the game at 14. After that, however, the wheels came off; Oregon State won, 56-26.

Summers, who became the defensive coordinator in 2025 and served as interim head coach after Jay Norvell was fired during the season, was one of the staff members Mora retained.

Mora coached the Falcons from 2004 through 2006 and the Seahawks in 2009. At the college level, he coached UCLA from 2012 through 2017 and Connecticut from 2022 through 2025.

item.title: Cardinals-Giants carries unexpected historical significance
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On the surface, Sunday's game between the Cardinals and the Giants brings little if any sizzle to the NFL menu.
item.content:encoded:
On the surface, Sunday's game between the Cardinals and the Giants brings little if any sizzle to the NFL menu. But there's a surprising amount of history embedded in the series.

Via NBC Sports research, the two teams first met 100 years ago next month, on November 7, 1926. Today's game will be the 130th time they've squared off.

From 1950 through 2001 (with the exception of 1968 and 1982), they played twice per year. Even after the Cardinals moved to Arizona, they remained in the NFC East for more than a decade.

Since the realignment of the divisions in 2002, they've played 11 times. Most recently, they met in 2023. The Giants won that one, 31-28; the Cardinals had won four in a row before that.

A win for the Giants would give them a 3-0 record at home for the first time since 2008. A win for the Cardinals would end a 16-game losing streak against teams that entered the contest with a losing record.

Of the eight games in the 1:00 p.m. ET window, it still doesn't generate a ton of excitement. But at least we tried.

item.title: Marcus Mariota injured, third-string quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis in for Commanders
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Commanders are down to their third-string quarterback today in London against the Colts.
item.content:encoded:
The Commanders are down to their third-string quarterback.

Second-string quarterback Marcus Mariota started today against the Colts in London because Jayden Daniels has an elbow injury, but in the first quarter Mariota was injured and walked to the locker room, replaced by third-stringer Athan Kaliakmanis.

The Commanders said Mariota is questionable to return with a right knee injury, which he suffered when Colts defensive lineman Laiatu Latu landed on Mariota's lower right leg and bent it awkwardly.

Kaliakmanis is a seventh-round rookie who played his college football at Rutgers and Minnesota.

item.title: One year later, Mark Sanchez criminal, civil cases are not yet resolved
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: One year ago today, news emerged that former NFL quarterback and Fox announcer Mark Sanchez had been stabbed multiple times while in Indianapolis to call a game between the Raiders and the Colts.
item.content:encoded:
One year ago today, news emerged that former NFL quarterback and Fox announcer Mark Sanchez had been stabbed multiple times while in Indianapolis to call a game between the Raiders and the Colts. As the hours passed, it became more and more clear that the authorities weren't regarding Sanchez as the victim but as the aggressor.

By Sunday afternoon, Sanchez faced assault charges for his altercation with Perry Tole, a 69-year-old truck driver.

Tole later sued Sanchez, Fox, and the parent company of St. Elmo's steakhouse. Fox eventually severed ties with Sanchez.

Through it all, the legal proceedings lingered. The criminal trial had been set for December 2025. It was delayed multiple times. As the latest date for the trial approached (September 8), news emerged that Sanchez planned to plead guilty.

More than a month later, Sanchez has yet to enter the revised plea. The specific charge to which Sanchez will plead guilty remains unclear.

As to the civil case, indications emerged that a settlement was in the works. No deal has been announced; the civil case returned to court on Friday for reasons that have not yet been disclosed or reported.

In the legal system, nothing is done until it's done. One year after the incident, nothing is done yet.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Eagles are reportedly making a change to their quarterback depth chart for Sunday's game against the Rams.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles are reportedly making a change to their quarterback depth chart for Sunday's game against the Rams.

Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that Tanner McKee will move up to the No. 2 spot behind Jalen Hurts. Andy Dalton had been in that role for the last three weeks.

Dalton was called on in Week 3 when Hurts had to be checked for a concussion with the Eagles driving in the second quarter. Dalton was picked off by Bears safety Dillon Thieneman in the end zone and the Eagles went on to lose 27-7 to fall to 2-1 on the year.

Jeff McLane of the Philadelphia Inquirer reports that both McKee and Dalton are expected to be active due to injuries that will force other players to the inactive list.

item.title: NFL will surely want to plug "hold-in" loophole, but it won't be easy
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: When the workers find real power, management can't take it.
item.content:encoded:
When the workers find real power, management can't take it.

Under the NFL's Collective Bargaining Agreement, the workers have found real power. In one very specific way.

The 2020 CBA made it much more difficult for players to hold out. Enter the hold-in.

In many cases, the team allows a player who wants a new contract to not practice while talks continue. The player is in the building (once a player reports it's difficult under the CBA to leave), he's working out, he's attending meetings. It's just a matter of time before a deal is done.

Unless a deal isn't done. And if the player is willing to cite an injury, embellished or flat-out fabricated, to refuse to provide services until the player gets what he wants, the team is stuck.

Last year, the Cowboys cried "uncle" after they realized that their apparent plan to kick the can on the Micah Parsons contract through the 2025 season wasn't going to work, because Parsons wasn't going to play, due to a back injury. This year, former Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. cited a back injury (which has suddenly healed, to no surprise) to sit out all of training camp, all of the preseason, and the first three games of the regular season. On Wednesday, the Steelers threw in the towel and traded Porter to, coincidentally, the Cowboys.

The powers-that-be won't like this trend, because the players have found a way to crack the code on the CBA. After years of playing football, any player could point to one or more body parts that create chronic pain and/or present a risk of more significant injury.

If a player is committed to the approach, what can the team do? Tell him they don't believe him? Fine him? Suspend him?

It would spark a legal mess under the CBA, a P.R. debacle for the team, and a potential morale issue in the locker room.

Enter the looming talks on a new labor deal. Surely, the Management Council is already brainstorming strategies to end the hold-in.

One fairly simple possibility would entail arranging for a neutral, third-party doctor to examine the player and to determine whether he has an injury and, if so, whether he shouldn't be practicing or playing because of it. If the doctor says the player is fine, and if the player persists in refusing to practice or play, the player becomes susceptible to an immediate fine, or a suspension.

Still, that's far easier said than done. Most competent doctors will tell patients that they know their bodies better than anyone. Most competent doctors aren't in the habit of telling patients they're faking a condition.

Really, who wants to be potentially responsible for informing a player he doesn't have a real injury and essentially forcing him to play when he doesn't want to?

The better approach could be to financially incentivize the player to practice and play. Over the past 20 years or so, offseason workout bonuses and per-game active roster bonuses have become an effective tool to tie pay to actual performance. A significant training-camp (and/or regular-season) practice participation bonus would raise the stakes for players who can't (or won't) suit up. Per-game active roster bonuses, which currently aren't part of the standard rookie deals, could be added to the formula for paying draft picks.

Obviously, this would punish players who are legitimately injured, and it would tempt some players to risk further injury in the name of earning their pay. But the teams already employ that approach with active-roster bonuses in veteran contracts. For young players, it becomes an important device to avoid a hold-in after their third seasons, when they become eligible for second contracts.

The problem is that the goalposts will potentially move. A player who wants a new contract and who previously would have cited an injury to avoid playing could just half-ass it through practices or games. But it's one thing to refuse to play; it's another to put on the uniform, step into the arena, and constantly make business decisions. That would open the player up to fair criticism from media and fans, and to resentment from his teammates.

Still, management has to be miffed that players have found a way to stage what is essentially a one-man wildcat strike until he gets what he wants. And it would be foolish to think the league isn't already trying to come up with a way to end it.

That said, some owners may not mind it. In 2025, the Cowboys' loss was Green Bay's gain, after the Packers traded for Parsons. In 2026, the Cowboys benefited from the tactic that was used against them last year, with the trade that brought Porter to Dallas.

Given that all owners could have their contractual rights to a player short-circuited by a conscious refusal to practice or play based on a non-existent injury, the overall balance likely tips in favor of trying to find a way to claw back the power the players have created by claiming, in an industry rife with injuries, that they aren't healthy enough to work — even if they are.

item.title: Daniel Jones fumbles, Commanders score first in London
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Commanders took a 3-0 lead just two minutes into the game.
item.content:encoded:
Colts quarterback Daniel Jones has had an ugly start in London today.

On the Colts' first play, Jones threw a pass that was batted down at the line of scrimmage. On the Colts' second play, Jones was sacked by Washington's Odafe Oweh, forcing a fumble that Oweh recovered.

The Commanders took over in great field position at the 21-yard line but couldn't gain a first down and settled for a 31-yard field Drew Stevens goal.

It's 3-0 Commanders, just two minutes into the game.

item.title: Steelers DL Derrick Harmon is expected to miss multiple weeks with foot injury
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Steelers defensive lineman Derrick Harmon had to be carted off during Thursday night's loss to the Browns and it looks like it will be a little while before he's back on the field.
item.content:encoded:
Steelers defensive lineman Derrick Harmon had to be carted off during Thursday night's loss to the Browns and it looks like it will be a little while before he's back on the field.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Harmon is expected to miss a few weeks with a foot injury. Injured reserve is a consideration for Harmon and he'd miss at least four games if the team goes that route.

The Steelers will play the Colts, Buccaneers, Saints and Browns before a bye in Week 9.

Harmon had 12 tackles, 1.5 sacks and a forced fumble in the first four weeks of the season. The 2025 first-rounder had 27 tackles, three sacks and a fumble recovery during his rookie season.

item.title: Report: Lions, Sam LaPorta break off contract extension talks
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The chances of tight end Sam LaPorta hitting free agency next year are reportedly looking a little better.
item.content:encoded:
The chances of tight end Sam LaPorta hitting free agency next year are reportedly looking a little better.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that LaPorta and the Lions have broken off talks on a contract extension. The 2023 second-round pick is in the final year of his rookie deal.

LaPorta and the Lions could revisit talks later in the season or early in the offseason. The team could also use the franchise tag to hold onto LaPorta, so it's not a sure thing that he'll be talking to other teams come March.

LaPorta has 14 catches for 144 yards and a touchdown so far this season.

item.title: Jalon Daniels: "Dream come true" to be starting QB for the Buccaneers today
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The undrafted rookie will start today against the Packers with Baker Mayfield out.
item.content:encoded:
During his six-year college career at Kansas, Jalon Daniels was never viewed as a sure thing to make it to the NFL. He certainly wasn't viewed as a prospect who was likely to be a starting quarterback in the NFL as a rookie.

But that's exactly what Daniels is today: The starting quarterback for the Buccaneers against the Packers. Baker Mayfield is out, and Daniels, an undrafted rookie, is the next man up. He says he's ready.

"I don't even know if I can put it into words," Daniels said. "It's a dream come true. It's a dream come true to even play for an NFL organization. To be able to go out there and have my first NFL start, it means everything."

As is usually the case for an undrafted rookie, Daniels had taken very few practice reps with the first-string offense until last week, when Mayfield was injured. But he says he has prepared like a starter.

"Every single week I prepare as if I'm going to get the starting reps," Daniels said.

The 0-3 Buccaneers desperately need a win. If Daniels can get it done, it will be one of the most surprising stories of this NFL season.

item.title: Deion Sanders, Colorado lose third in a row
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: After a 2-0 start to the 2026 season, Deion Sanders and the Colorado Buffaloes have lost their third game in a row.
item.content:encoded:
After a 2-0 start to the 2026 season, Deion Sanders and the Colorado Buffaloes have lost their third game in a row.

The latest loss came at home to No. 10 Texas Tech, 29-7.

Colorado led at the half, 7-3. The Red Raiders pulled away after intermission.

The Buffaloes had turnovers on four straight possessions.

Colorado scored on its opening drive of the game and didn't score again thereafter.

Isaac Wilson, the brother of NFL quarterback Zach Wilson, started at quarterback over Julian Lewis. Wilson threw three interceptions on the night.

For the Buffaloes, the season-opening win at Georgia Tech is a fading memory. Next up for Colorado are games against No. 13 Utah and No. 19 Oklahoma State. Which means that 2-3 could become 2-5.

If the current trend continues, it's fair to wonder whether Deion will return for a fifth season in 2027.

item.title: Jeremiah Smith: "I'm the best player in the country"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: After his latest phenomenal performance of the 2026 season, Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith stated the obvious.
item.content:encoded:
After his latest phenomenal performance of the 2026 season, Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith stated the obvious.

"You've just got to [let] the Heisman voters or whoever it is know that I’m the best player in the country," Smith said, via Adam Rittenberg of ESPN. "I've got to be there."

In the Buckeyes' 31-14 win over Iowa, Smith broke the Ohio State record for career receptions with 207 and career touchdown catches with 36.

He also tied the program record with his 15th career 100-yard game.

In five games this season, Smith has 44 catches for 617 yards and nine touchdowns. Against the Hawkeyes (not the Hawks), Smith had 11 catches for 206 yards and two touchdowns.

Smith NIL deal surely requires him to keep playing. As it relates to his NFL prospects, however, the hay is in the barn. He could stop playing right now and still be one of the top picks in the 2027 draft.

item.title: Yale QB Dante Reno has big performance after his father (and former coach) dies
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Yale quarterback Dante Reno had a performance on Saturday he'll never forget, for many reasons.
item.content:encoded:
Yale quarterback Dante Reno had a performance on Saturday he'll never forget, for many reasons.

Reno threw for 298 yards and four touchdown passes in a come-from-behind win over Merrimack. The game happened one day after Yale announced the passing of former football head coach Tony Reno, who was Dante's father.

"This one's for you pops," Dante Reno said on Twitter.

Merrimack led Yale 21-7 in the second quarter. Fueled by Dante Reno's performance, the Bulldogs outscored Merrimack 34-3 to win the game.

Tony Reno, who coached his son in 2025, stepped down in February 2026, citing health reasons. Tony Reno won the second-most games in Yale history, with 83. He coached Yale from 2012 through 2025, winning five Ivy League titles.

"Dad, you are my role model, my best friend and my coach," Dante Reno wrote when his father stepped down. "I love you so much. The last 15 years you have been the best head coach I have ever seen. From your first year to playing with you last year, you have put your heart and soul into coaching. Your legacy will last forever."

Tony Reno was 52 years old.

item.title: Tyson Bagent is expected to start for the Bears on Sunday vs. Jets
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Case Keenum will take a seat on the bench, after beating the Eagles on Monday night.
item.content:encoded:
The Bears are deferring to their depth chart.

Despite Monday night's win by third-string quarterback Case Keenum over the Eagles, the Bears will apparently turn to second-stringer Tyson Bagent on Sunday against the Jets.

Via Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Bagent is expected to start the game.

Although the Bears have tried to keep the identity of the starter a secret, the signs have pointed to Bagent. He took the first-team reps during practice on Wednesday and Thursday — and possibly Friday.

Coach Ben Johnson hasn't announced a starter for the Week 4 game. Does he need to? Bagent is listed as the backup to starter Caleb Williams. Bagent didn't play on Monday night, given that he was able to practice all week while in the concussion protocol.

Keenum got the Week 3 start against the Eagles. With Bagent cleared, the Bears have decided not to ignore the preordained configuration of quarterbacks, even though Keenum managed to engineer a 27-7 win over the Eagles.

Undrafted out of Shepherd, Bagent started four games in 2023, his rookie year. He has made eight appearances since then. Most recently, he replaced Williams in the fourth quarter of the Week 2 loss to the Vikings. Bagent nearly pulled off the victory.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes looks to extend mastery of Raiders, AFC West
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: When the Chiefs play in Las Vegas on Sunday, Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes will be looking to extend his mastery of the Raiders — and of their division.
item.content:encoded:
When the Chiefs play in Las Vegas on Sunday, Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes will be looking to extend his mastery of the Raiders — and of their division.

Via NBC Sports research, Mahomes has a career record of 13-2 against the Raiders. In those 15 games, Mahomes has thrown 36 touchdown passes against five interceptions.

Mahomes is also 7-0 on the road against the Raiders, with 20 touchdown passes and two interceptions in those games.

Against the AFC West, Mahomes has a record of 37-8. The 82.2 percent winning rate is the best for any quarterback since the merger against division rivals, based on a minimum of 25 starts.

This year could be different. The Raiders are 3-0, as are the Chiefs. The winner will move to 4-0 and take early control of the division.

item.title: Mack Hollins fined twice on the same play, losing $34,441
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The NFL fined Patriots receiver Mack Hollins $34,441 for his actions on the same play against the Jaguars.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL fined Patriots receiver Mack Hollins $34,441 for his actions on the same play against the Jaguars.

Hollins was docked $11,941 for taunting and $22,500 for unnecessary roughness involving his helmet.

With 13:32 left in the fourth quarter, Hollins caught a 9-yard pass on third-and-10. Officials threw a flag for taunting after he gestured toward Jaguars safety Eric Murray.

He was not penalized for illegal use of the helmet.

Hollins led the Patriots with six catches for 87 yards.

After a January 2025 game against the Broncos, the league fined him twice for taunting. He lost $11,255 for stepping over cornerback Patrick Surtain and $6,736 for standing over receiver Marvin Mims after a punt.

item.title: Jaylen Waddle was fined $14,926 for dice roll, too
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Do as we say, not as we profit from.
item.content:encoded:
Do as we say, not as we profit from.

Like Broncos guard Quinn Meinerz, who was fined $14,926 for a forbidden celebratory dice roll, Broncos receiver Jaylen Waddle was fined the same amount for the same celebration on the same play.

The moment came after Waddle caught a third-quarter touchdown pass in Denver's eventual win over the Rams. The description of the infraction in the league's weekly announcement of fines is "[i]llegal celebrations and vulgar acts."

It the latest example of the NFL's sudden return to its No-Fun-League ways. Indeed, the NFL had no issue with former Steelers receiver Martavis Bryant pretending to roll dice after scoring a touchdown in 2017 — and that was before the Supreme Court opened the floodgates for legalized sports betting and the NFL decided to abandon its loathing of gambling and open its arms to grab as much cash as it can.

This season, the league is grabbing cash from players for doing things that used to be OK. Undoubtedly, the players will aggressively appeal.

The only good news is that the fine money, if collected, goes to charity.

item.title: Week 3 featured three fines for blindside blocks, two fines for hip-drop tackles
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The NFL's announcement of fines for Week 3 featured six infractions for player safety fouls that qualify toward possible suspensions.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL's announcement of fines for Week 3 featured six infractions for player safety fouls that qualify toward possible suspensions.

Two of those fouls were hip-drop tackles. 49ers linebacker Fred Warner and Rams safety Kam Curl were each fined $17,911. Warner was also fined $23,882 for illegal use of his helmet in a tackle.

Texans linebacker Jamal Hill, Giants tight end Isaiah Likely, and Steelers linebacker Cole Holcomb were each fined for blindside blocks. Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was fined for a hit on a defenseless player.

Any player with three fines for any one of those infractions will be suspended for one game. The same potential penalty applies to fouls for launching or horse-collar tackles. No player has been fined more than once for any of the qualifying infractions yet this season.

item.title: Stephen Jones: Steelers' initial asking price for Joey Porter Jr. was "a little hefty"
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Cowboys Executive V.P.
item.content:encoded:
Cowboys Executive V.P. Stephen Jones says the team spent significant time negotiating a trade with the Steelers for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. that made sense for the Cowboys — and made the trade only after the Steelers' price came down.

Jones said on 105.3 The Fan that what the Steelers were initially asking for was more than the Cowboys were willing to give up, but they eventually got the Steelers to lower the price to a 2027 sixth-round pick and 2028 second-round pick.

"Early on the price was a little hefty for us, then it got to a point where we could deal with it," Jones said.

Jones said the Cowboys know there's a chance Porter will leave in free agency after this season, but they think if he does, they'll get a 2028 compensatory pick that largely makes up for losing the 2028 second-round pick.

"We had to have that trade make sense if Joey left after this year," Jones said. "That's why the 2 in '28 matches up with a compensatory pick. If he did leave we'd probably get a 3 or a 4 for him and get that back for Joey in '28 when that 2 is in place. So it made a lot of sense. It protected us."

Even if Porter proves to be only a rental for the rest of this season before going elsewhere, Jones thinks the price was right, once the Steelers lowered it.

item.title: YouTube believes NFL could "deconstruct" Sunday Ticket in next broadcast deals
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Come 2030, out-of-market games could be seen without plunking down an extra $400.
item.content:encoded:
The next wave of NFL broadcast deals could include plenty of changes. One change could be the end of the out-of-market package of games.

Via Alex Sherman of CNBC, YouTube believes that the NFL could “deconstruct” Sunday Ticket.

The league first launched Sunday Ticket in 1994, marketing it as a way for fans to watch games not televised in the markets where they reside. DirecTV owned the package for years, before YouTube acquired the rights in 2023.

The current Sunday Ticket deal with YouTube, for which the company pays $2 billion per year, remains the subject of a federal class action that is pending on appeal in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, The case could still result in a massive liability for the NFL (in excess of $14 billion). It also could generate a court order compelling the NFL to end the longstanding device for allowing fans to watch all games played in the Sunday afternoon windows.

The NFL lost at trial in 2024. The jury found that the NFL's pricing of the package, which was intended to be high enough to persuade many viewers to choose to watch the CBS and Fox games available in their local markets, violated the antitrust laws.

The judge didn't throw out the entire verdict; he dismissed the damages award. The finding of an antitrust violation remains in place — and it continues.

At some point, there likely will be a reckoning. And the league has already explored the possibility of making the games available through other platforms, simulating a college football viewing experience that has a wide variety of games on various cable and broadcast platforms.

Quite possibly, the league could make as much or more money by selling in-market games to a pair of broadcast networks, with the out-of-market games sprinkled throughout the various other channels on the dial.

Regardless of the revenue potential, the league will have no choice, if a court compels them to dismantle Sunday Ticket. And it would allow fans to watch games on networks to which they already have access, without paying nearly $400 per year for it.

Ditching Sunday Ticket would also address concerns that the league has devalued it by putting more and more games into non-Sunday windows. And it would give the NFL the freedom to more aggressively schedule games for Wednesday nights and, eventually, Tuesday nights.
